transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what really scared me enough to ask for help is that... lately, I keep having these mornings where I just think it might be easier if I didn't wake up. I want to be clear that I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But just having that thought cross my mind was enough to make me realize I should probably come in and talk to someone.
Can you tell me how long you've been having these low feelings and thoughts about not wanting to wake up—has this been going on for days, weeks, or longer?
It's been about a month. Um, my sister died unexpectedly about a month ago, and... well, that's really when these feelings started.
Besides these low mornings, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—like hobbies, socializing, or work—nearly every day over this past month?

Yes, I have. I mean, I still make myself show up for things, like my book club or the dance night I go to. But lately, I just sit there feeling like I'm behind a pane of glass. And even the quiet things at home... like working in my garden, or cooking for the neighbors... they just don't give me that little lift they used to.
Would you say these low, empty feelings and loss of enjoyment are with you most of the day, nearly every day, or do they mainly come up when something reminds you of your sister?

It's really most of the day, nearly every day. I mean, of course, it hits me harder when I think about her, but... that empty feeling is just sort of always there in the background now, no matter what I'm doing.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite over this past month—such as trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or eating much more or less than usual?

My sleep has definitely been affected. Um, I tend to fall asleep in bits and pieces now. And then I end up waking up well before dawn, and my mind is already turning. Once I'm awake like that, I usually can't get settled again before the day starts. I haven't really noticed much of a change with my appetite, though.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty about things—beyond just missing your sister or wishing you could have done something differently for her?

Well, it's mostly about her, honestly. I just... I keep going over those last few weeks in my head. I keep telling myself I should have called her more often, or that I should have listened better when we did talk. I feel like I should have done something more useful for her. I mean, part of me knows I couldn't have actually changed what happened, but... I just feel so guilty about it all the time.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy level or increased fatigue, or trouble concentrating on tasks, nearly every day over this past month?

Yes, I have. I just feel so tired all the time. Even simple errands or... getting the papers together for the Cultural Center, it all just leaves me feeling completely worn out. It's like my body is moving through thick mud. I haven't really noticed any trouble concentrating, though, it's mostly just the fatigue.
Would you say these feelings have made it hard for you to keep up with your usual responsibilities—like work, household tasks, or relationships—beyond what you'd expect from grieving your sister?

Yes, I think it has. I've actually had to ask another volunteer to cover parts of the Juneteenth budgeting workshop for me. I just... I can't seem to keep up with the preparation the way I normally would. And as for relationships, I've been turning down my neighbors and friends a lot more than usual lately when they ask to get together.
